turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): hey, vitals real quick before Dr. Patel. edge of the table, no hopping.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): I can walk. this is dumb.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): blood pressure one oh eight over sixty eight, pulse 92, temp 98.4, oxygen ninety nine percent. you're good.
[SEG0004] person_3 (DOCTOR): hi, I'm Dr. Patel. what's going on?
[SEG0005] person_2 (PATIENT): nothing. I just twisted my ankle.
[SEG0006] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): soccer yesterday. he planted funny and rolled it, walked off on his own, coach still pulled him. he's been shrugging it off ever since.
[SEG0007] person_3 (DOCTOR): which ankle are we talking about?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): right. it's fine.
[SEG0009] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): right ankle, the outside of it. swelled up within an hour, I swear.
[SEG0010] person_3 (DOCTOR): can you bear weight on it? like, actually walk?
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): yeah. since yesterday. hurts a little when I walk. so what.
[SEG0012] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): he did four steps in from the parking lot. limping, but he did them.
[SEG0013] person_3 (DOCTOR): any numbness, or tingling, in the toes?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): mm, I suppose. sometimes, not really.
[SEG0015] person_3 (DOCTOR): okay, that's a maybe, I'm not writing down numbness. let me press on it.

[SEG0016] person_3 (DOCTOR): there's swelling over the lateral ankle and a little bruise coming in. I'm on the posterior edge of the lateral malleolus and the medial one. bone, or the soft part in front?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): soft part. bone's fine.
[SEG0018] person_3 (DOCTOR): navicular up here, and the base of the fifth metatarsal. those sore?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): no.

[SEG0020] person_3 (DOCTOR): alright, Ottawa ankle rules, thinking out loud so you hear it. he bore weight right after and he can do four steps now, no tenderness on the posterior malleoli, navicular's quiet, fifth metatarsal base is quiet. so no x-ray today.
[SEG0021] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): um, last spring they x-rayed the other ankle at urgent care.
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): they said it was borderline.
[SEG0023] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): yeah, the guy called it borderline, maybe a tiny chip, didn't treat it like a real break. that was the left one.
[SEG0024] person_3 (DOCTOR): got it. old left ankle x-ray, they told you borderline, I'm not taking that as a confirmed fracture. doesn't change this ankle. any allergies to medicines?
[SEG0025] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): no, none that I know of.
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't take medicine.
[SEG0027] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I did give him ibuprofin this morning though. two hundred milligrams, one tablet. he made a face and swallowed it.
[SEG0028] person_3 (DOCTOR): then we'll keep ibuprofen at two hundred milligrams by mouth every six to eight hours, with food, only when it actually hurts, for a few days.
[SEG0029] person_3 (DOCTOR): rest it, ice maybe twenty minutes at a time, use a compression wrap but don't crank it tight, prop the ankle up when you sit. and no soccer until I say so.
[SEG0030] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): if the nurse wants him back, does he fast or something?
[SEG0031] person_3 (DOCTOR): no fasting. the nurse sees him Thursday morning at eight thirty to recheck the swelling and re-wrap. that's booked, not a maybe. just wear a shoe he can slip off.
[SEG0032] person_1 (NURSE): Thursday at 8:30, I'll book it on the way out. yep.
[SEG0033] person_3 (DOCTOR): and I'll see you in two weeks, in clinic. that one's on the schedule too.

[SEG0034] person_3 (DOCTOR): if he can't bear weight, or the swelling's clearly worse, then we do an x-ray. if it hasn't settled when I see you in two weeks, we might do a scan, only if it doesn't settle.
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): it's not even bad.
[SEG0036] person_3 (DOCTOR): you're minimizing, I get it. working impression is a lateral ankle sprain, provisional, and a fracture is unlikely on those Ottawa findings. take it easy.

spec.situation: Young player who twisted the ankle yesterday; swelling, can bear weight with pain; doctor applies Ottawa rules aloud, no X-ray unless it worsens; rest and elevation advice.

traps.happens: In the plan the doctor books some tests or visits for a definite time ('the nurse takes bloods Thursday morning', 'I'll see you in two weeks') and makes others conditional ('if those are borderline we do the third test', 'if it does not settle, a scan').
traps.label_rule: Booked or arranged = status planned. Only the hedged ones are conditional. Never mark a booked test conditional or 'if needed'. Instructions for the booked test (fasting, time, medicine timing) belong to that test's action, not a separate invented plan item.

features: test_result_recalled: the patient reports an old test or result ('they said it was borderline'); recorded as reported history/investigation only as far as said, not as a confirmed value.
ambiguous_answer: an answer that sounds like yes but is really 'maybe' ('mm, I suppose', 'sometimes, not really'); recorded with uncertainty or not at all, never as a firm fact.

omissions.text: Possible numbness/tingling in the toes was asked about; patient gave an equivocal answer ('sometimes, not really'), and the doctor explicitly decided not to record numbness.
Prior ibuprofen use this morning was as a single 200 mg tablet given by family member before the visit.
No right ankle x-ray is planned today based on Ottawa ankle rules.

Past history clarification: prior imaging was of the LEFT ankle last spring, described by urgent care as 'borderline, maybe a tiny chip,' and Dr. Patel stated this should not be taken as a confirmed fracture.
